Second Reading of the IMDA (Amendment) Bill

Second Reading6 May 2026 bill-797

A Second Reading debate on a Bill to amend the Info-communications Media Development Authority Act and make related amendments to the Telecommunications Act, aligning media-sector regulation with telecommunications regulation.

The Bill would require IMDA approval for acquisitions of 30% or more of a regulated media entity and allow IMDA to issue directions on market conduct and consumer protection. It would also allow the Minister to order structural separation as a last resort. The record does not set out specific price, service or employment outcomes.

  • Mr Tan Kiat How

    • The Bill aligns the media-sector regulatory framework with the telecommunication sector.

      Verbatim
      Principally, the amendments align the regulatory framework for the media sector with that for the telecommunication sector.

    • Under the amended ownership framework, IMDA prior approval would apply where a person acquires 30% or more interest, obtains effective control, or takes over a media business as a going concern.

      Verbatim
      Specifically, this would apply where a person acquires 30% or more interest in a regulated person, obtains effective control over its operations, or takes over its media business as a going concern.

    • Clause 6 empowers IMDA to issue directions for fair and efficient market conduct or to safeguard consumers' interests.

      Verbatim
      Clause 6 of the Bill empowers IMDA to issue directions for the purposes of maintaining fair and efficient market conduct or to safeguard consumers' interests by promoting fair, transparent and reliable provision of media services.

    • Clause 15 vests the power to order structural separation in the Minister rather than IMDA.

      Verbatim
      clause 15 provides that the powers to order structural separation of a regulated person is vested in the Minister rather than IMDA.

    • Clause 3 updates the definition of parties who can be designated as regulated persons.

      Verbatim
      clause 3 updates the definition of parties who can be designated as regulated persons to address potential gaps.

    • Clause 5 allows IMDA to approve documents prepared by a person other than IMDA as a code of practice or standard of performance.

      Verbatim
      clause 5 allows IMDA to approve documents prepared by a person other than IMDA as a code of practice or standard of performance for the media sector.

    • The amendment for immaterial transactions is intended to lighten the regulatory burden and align with the telecom sector.

      Verbatim
      This amendment will lighten the regulatory burden and align the approach taken for the telecom sector.

    • Clause 18 makes related amendments to the Telecommunications Act for alignment purposes.

      Verbatim
      clause 18 makes related amendments to the Telecommunications Act itself.

  • Mr Sharael Taha

    • Mr Sharael Taha supported the Bill to strengthen competition, protect consumers and keep the media ecosystem fair, vibrant and resilient.

      Verbatim
      I rise in support of this Bill to strengthen competition, protect consumers and ensure that our media ecosystem remains fair, vibrant and resilient.

    • Mr Sharael Taha said that broader regulatory powers require clearer guardrails.

      Verbatim
      When regulatory powers become broader, the guardrails must become clearer.

    • Mr Sharael Taha described the Bill as moving from regulating behaviour to shaping market structure.

      Verbatim

      Verbatim

Motion on AI-enabled growth and support for workers and enterprises

5 May 2026 – 6 May 2026 motion-2970, motion-2976, motion-2978

A Motion moved by Mr Ng Chee Meng setting out four commitments on AI-enabled economic growth, fairness, worker and enterprise support, and inclusive progress, followed by debate and a ministerial response.

The transcript sets out measures that affect workers and businesses: from the second half of this year, Singaporeans enrolled in selected SkillsFuture AI courses will receive six months of free access to premium AI tools; eligible businesses will receive $10,000 under the redesigned SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit later this year; and all IHLs will offer selected AI-related courses for alumni at a significant discount for a year starting in the second half of this year. It also records that the Government will study improvements to the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme and that tripartite partners are discussing shortening retrenchment notification under the Employment Act review.

Adjournment Motion on a national energy resilience strategy using solar and battery microgrids

Adjournment Motion6 May 2026 matter-adj-2980

An Adjournment Motion moved by Mr Azhar Othman proposing a national energy resilience strategy based on decentralised off-grid and micro-grid power solutions with solar photovoltaic generation and battery energy storage, followed by a response from Minister of State Gan Siow Huang.

Mr Azhar Othman said public housing estates, which house 80% of our population, largely lack any form of backup beyond emergency lighting in stairwells, and that when the grid fails lifts and water pumps stop. He proposed that solar plus battery storage keep essential loads such as lifts and water pumps running during outages. Ms Gan Siow Huang said microgrids are one of several distributed energy solutions that will be studied further, subject to safety requirements and technical standards.

      Verbatim

      Verbatim

      Verbatim

How this page was made

Built from the official Hansard record (Parliament of Singapore Official Reports). No news reporting was used. Briefs are written by software from the transcript and every key point carries the verbatim words it was drawn from.

  • Reports collected: 138 of about 144 (96%)
  • Briefs on this page: 3 (117 verified points)
  • Speaker attribution: 96% of turns carry an explicit speaker tag
  • Any point whose quote could not be found in the transcript was discarded rather than shown.
  • Coverage is below 100%. Some items from this sitting may be missing, so read the totals as a floor rather than a final count.
